items.title: George Avakian interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 21, 1998
items.q: He added Lionel Hampton on vibraphone, and the Goodman quartet was formed.

ctx.x: But it doesn’t matter. And the great breakthrough came about in the middle 30s when Benny Goodman hired Teddy Wilson to play as a member of the first Goodman trio that started on records actually. But Goodman decided we’re going to do this in person. So what he did was to play a set and maybe twice an evening, they would do this at the end of the set there would be a brief break and out would come the trio with Teddy replacing Jess Stacy on piano and Gene Krupa returning to the drums, and they would play maybe…
It wasn’t just in the south either, was it? © Fillius Jazz Archive -7-
